newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russians evacuated from Tirana, ambassador stays.
newsitem.headline: Russians evacuated from Tirana, ambassador stays.

text.p: A group of Russian evacuees left Tirana on U.S. military helicopters on Saturday, Itar-Tass news agency said.
A Foreign Ministry source said Moscow's ambassador to Albania Igor Saprykin had accompanied the evacuees to the American embassy but was not planning to leave himself for the time being.

"The Russian ambassador is with a group of embassy people in the American embassy complex to supervise the evacuation. After that he will return to the (Russian) embassy. So far it is not planned that he should leave," the source said by telephone.
He was unable to confirm the evacuation had taken place and Tass did not say how many people had left.
A Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Thursday there were nearly 300 Russians living in Albania and that it was evacuating 14 diplomatic family members because of the unrest.

United States military helicopters resumed their operation evacuating American citizens from the Albanian capital at dawn on Saturday. It had been suspended on Friday after two Marine Cobra helicopters came under ground fire.
A U.S. military spokesman said 89 people had been brought out of a total of 200 due to be evacuated during the day.

On Saturday President Boris Yeltsin ordered the ministry to draw up a timetable for the evacuation of diplomats and other Russians wishing to leave in coordination with the foreign intelligence services and emergencies ministry.

Albania, Europe's poorest nation, slid towards anarchy this week as rebels looted arms depots across the country and an anti-government uprising sparked by the collapse of pyramid savings schemes gathered pace.
